newsitem.title: USA: Calif health care reform to hit L.A. - opponents say.
newsitem.headline: Calif health care reform to hit L.A. - opponents say.

text.p: Health care reform measures on California's November ballot would impose tens of millions of dollars of new costs on Los Angeles city and county, opponents of two measures warned on Wednesday.

At a news conference at Childrens Hospital of Los Angeles, opponents of Propositions 214 and 216 said a recent study had identified $54.5 million in additional costs to Los Angeles city and county and to the Los Angeles Unified School District should the initiatives pass.

"At a minimum, the hit on Los Angeles city and county agencies will be at least tens of millions of dollars annually, and that doesn't even factor in the costs to the private sector which run millions of dollars more," said Allan Zaremberg, executive vice president of the California Chamber of Commerce, one of the groups opposed to the propositions.
Opponents at the Los Angeles news conference also said the measures would require a huge bureaucracy to administer.
"This all but takes away the ability of hospitals to efficiently manage patient services," said Mary Dee Hacker, vice president of patient care services at Childrens Hospital.
According to the Secretary of State, Propositions 214 would, among its many provisions, prohibit health care businesses from offering incentives for withholding care.

Proposition 216 would, in addition to prohibiting businesses from offering incentives for withholding care, establish a non-profit corporation to advocate for health care consumers, the Secretary of State said.
The initiatives will appear on the November 5 state ballot.
